title: Beef keema with white cabbage and potatoes

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple; curry powder, tinned tomatoes and yoghurt are ordinary cupboard and fridge items.

supermarket.reason: Beef mince, cabbage, potatoes, curry powder and natural yoghurt are everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one lidded casserole, a peeler, a knife and a wooden spoon, and the technique is simple frying and simmering.

works.reason: 500g mince, 500g potatoes and 500g cabbage feed four. The 2cm potato chunks get about 30 minutes in liquid so will be tender. The tomatoes and 300ml water reduce to a thick keema once cooked uncovered, and 2 tbsp curry powder with a tsp of salt seasons it well.

honest_times.reason: Slicing two onions, peeling and chunking the potatoes and shredding half a cabbage, plus about 18 minutes at the hob, fits roughly 30 minutes hands-on. The 55 minutes total holds if the potatoes and cabbage are prepped while the onions soften.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and the optional cavolo nero in the tip is on the March fresh list.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming one-pot curry suits a chilly early March evening. Half a cabbage is a main component of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear and neighbourly in British English. The intro's 'White cabbage from store' reads a little oddly and could become 'Stored white cabbage', but it does not get in the way.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family meal of mince, potatoes, plenty of cabbage and tomatoes, topped with yoghurt.
